the differential entropy approximation used for the information theoretic approach is a very powerful tool that can be used to construct a wide variety of contrast functions for IKA, that the resulting estimators are statistically optimal under certain conditions, and that fixed-point algorithms can be derived for their practical implementation.

we introduce a family new contrast functions for linear ICA that are based on maximum entropy approximations to differential entropy, and that we introduce fast fixed-point algorithms for their minimization.

1) The differential entropy approximation used in our contrast functions has good statistical properties, and the resulting contrast functions are robust and have minimum variance under the assumption that the data are generated by a linear mixture of statistically independent components; 2) We introduce a new family of contrast functions for linear ICA that can be optimized by fixed-point iterations; 3) We introduce a simple and fast fixed-point algorithm for ICA, which is robust and of minimum variance under the linear mixture assumption.
